newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: CRICKET-PAKISTAN FAIL TO RAM HOME ADVANTAGE.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-PAKISTAN FAIL TO RAM HOME ADVANTAGE.

text.p: New Zealand made a solid start to their bid to rescue the second test on Saturday after Pakistan made 430 in their first innings to take a 181-run lead.
Bryan Young and Justin Vaughan survived numerous lbw appeals in the closing session to steer their side to 69 without loss.
Young was on 38 and Vaughan 26 at the end of an absorbing third day in which Pakistan fell apart after looking set for a huge total.
Their last six wickets fell for just 54 runs after solid early partnerships.

Much tighter New Zealand bowling took wickets at regular intervals after Chris Cairns removed Pakistani captain Saeed Anwar for 149. His fine innings included 20 boundaries over a span of 214 balls and 305 minutes.
Anwar mistimed a hook off a short delivery and Simon Doull took an excellent catch at long leg.
Mushtaq Ahmed amassed a test-best 42 and veteran Salim Malik went for 78.
Cairns was by far the most dangerous, if most expensive, New Zealand bowler. He finished with five for 137 off 30.4 overs, but could face a penalty for showing dissent.
Malik was on 27 when umpire Javed Akhtar turned down a very vociferous appeal from Cairns, who continued to press his case.

On Friday, Pakistan's Ejaz Ahmed was fined half his match fee after Akhtar pronounced him lbw for 125. Ejaz waved his bat at the umpire in a vain attempt to signal that the ball had touched it before hitting his pad.
